ask: Horizontal inspection of the crew runtime: read crew/ as one system and report where it is inconsistent with itself, where it duplicates itself, and what can be simplified without changing behaviour. Concretely: helpers that exist in two or more of crew.mjs, drive.mjs, seat-io.mjs, daemon.mjs, child.mjs, factoryctl.mjs under different names or with drift between copies; refusal and absence grammar that differs between modules for the same situation (an error string shaped one way here and another way there; a null meaning 'unmeasured' in one reducer and 'zero' in another); exported symbols with no importer outside their own test; closed enums declared in more than one place; functions over 150 lines whose branches could be tables; places where a later module re-derives what an earlier one already recorded in crew.json or the journal. Every finding names file:line on both sides and says what the simplification is and what test pins it today.
done_means: A ranked findings register. Each finding: the two-or-more locations (file:line), the category (duplicate / grammar-drift / dead-export / oversize / re-derivation), the proposed simplification in one sentence, the test that pins current behaviour or the statement that none does, and a cost estimate in files touched. Ranked by (behaviour risk of the inconsistency) then (lines removed). Every claim verified by reading the code, never inferred from names — a helper with the same name and different semantics is a finding in its own right, not a duplicate. Dead-export claims are checked with a grep across the whole checkout including tests and skills, and the grep is quoted. The register says which of the eleven files were read in full and which were sampled.
out_of_scope: No edits. No proposals that change behaviour, journal events, enum members or CLI flags. No opinions about naming that are not also an inconsistency. Protected-floor files may be named in findings but the register must flag them as judge-tier. Tests are another scout's surface — name a test only as the pin for a runtime finding.
